1wxw7sx:381: The standard LLM-as-a-Judge method prompts the model to output a discrete score token (e.g., 1-8), then selects the highest-probability token as the final score. However, when comparing complex long-horizon agent trajectories, this coarse-grained scoring often assigns the same score to two trajectories (e.g., both get 4), leading to ties that cannot be resolved. Experimental data show that LLM-as-a-Judge produces a tie rate as high as 27% on Terminal-Bench. This is a fatal flaw in scenarios that require fine-grained selection of the best trajectory, such as code generation and terminal operations. The core idea of LLM-as-a-Verifier is to distinguish the “Judge” (forming an overall judgment and giving a decision) from the “Verifier” (confirming the correctness of something, requiring more detailed assessment). Instead of outputting a coarse-grained score, the verifier provides fine-grained feedback by expanding three dimensions: scoring granularity, number of repeated verifications, and evaluation criteria decomposition.
